newsitem.title: UK: Welcome Break taps bond market for 321 million stg.
newsitem.headline: Welcome Break taps bond market for 321 million stg.

text.p: Welcome Break, a chain of British motorway service stations owned by Bahrain-based INVESTCORP, on Tuesday issued bonds worth 321 million stg to refinance its short-term debt.
Loans taken out for Welcome Break Group Ltd's 476 million stg purchase earlier this year of 21 service stations will be repaid with the deal.
The highly structured issue has been touted for some weeks. It involved the launch of four bonds, two fixed-rate and two FRNs, secured by cashflows from the operation of the service stations.
Credit enhancement was provided, in the first instance, by cashflow overcollateralization.
Standard and Poors Corp rated 254 million stg of the offering at A and the balance at BBB.
A 45 million stg revolving facility, rated A by S&P, was also made available by Welcome Break Finance Plc, a special purpose vehicle in whose name the bonds were launched, to Welcome Break.
S&P said the deal was a secured loan structure as opposed to a true sale of assets to the issuer.

It said an integrated approach had been adopted, whereby the rating of the notes was based, among other things, on the underlying corporate business risk assessment of the borrower together with structural enhancements to ensure timely repayment of the rated obligations.
Bankers Trust and Chase Manhattan were joint arrangers of the deal, while BZW was a co-lead arranger.

Welcome Break's primary assets are full ownership and operation of (or an interest in companies that own and operate) a total of 21 motorway service areas which include travel lodges, petrol, catering and retail outlets, and car parking areas.
Granada Plc was the prior owner.
